ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: a hunting season
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Six days of hunting: each morning the hunters find two head of the land's game marked for them, the biggest that is safe to hunt, so meat is laid by before the cold. A tribe keeps the hunters' moon, a village opens the season, an industrial colony takes out its game licence and a spacer colony calls it a cull; it comes to the same thing. The hunters are out more and at other work less, and a hunted animal may turn on them as the game has it. Hunters and the bloodthirsty like it; the kind, and those whose ideoligion holds hunting or violence wrong, mind it.

effects.li: Each morning for six days, two head of the land's game are marked for the hunters: the biggest that's safe, never a predator or anything likely to turn.
The hunters go out for them as the game sends hunters, and a hunted animal may still fight back.
Hunters, gourmands and the bloodthirsty like it; the kind mind it, and those whose ideoligion holds hunting or violence wrong hate it.

plain.li: The cold is coming and the meat store is half empty, so let the hunters go out every day.
[tribal] It's the hunters' moon, and every camp of my people would be out after the herds by now.
[medieval] Open the season, and we'll have salt meat in the cellar by the first frost.
[industrial] A week of hunting, and the smokehouse full before the snow.
[spacer] A short cull while the herds are fat would keep the freezer full through the winter.

blunt.li: There's meat walking about out there and we're eating oats.

cheerful.li: Out at first light every morning, I can't wait.

cold.li: Game is food we don't have to grow.

plain.li: Two a day for six days is a lot of the land's animals.
I'd rather the hunters went out when we need meat, not every morning by rule.

warm.li: The herds come back to that meadow every year, and I like seeing them there.

gloomy.li: Somebody will get gored, and then we'll stop.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: wood for the winter
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Eight days of felling: each morning up to six of the nearest wild trees outside the home area are marked for the cutters, until the stores hold the wood the winter wants (150 a colonist for a tribe or a village that burns it in every hearth, 80 for an industrial or spacer colony that wants it for its benches and generators). The cutters are at the trees and at nothing else. The industrious and the tough like it; the lazy mind it, and those whose ideoligion holds trees sacred hate it.

effects.li: Each morning for eight days, up to six of the nearest wild trees outside the home area are marked for the cutters, until the stores hold the winter's wood: 150 a colonist for a tribe or a village, 80 for any other colony.
The cutters fell them as the game has cutters do, and the wood waits for the haulers.
The industrious and the tough like it; the lazy mind it, and those whose ideoligion holds trees sacred hate it.

plain.li: The woodpile won't see us to spring, so let's fill it while the ground is dry.
[lowtech] Every hearth burns wood all winter, and we'd better have it cut before the snow.
[!lowtech] The benches and the generators eat timber, and the forest is right there.

blunt.li: Cold people don't work, so cut the wood.

cheerful.li: Nothing like an axe in autumn to warm you up.

cold.li: Wood now costs a week; wood in midwinter costs fingers.

plain.li: Eight days of nothing but trees, and the rest of the work piling up behind them.

warm.li: That stand of trees by the stream is the prettiest thing on the land.

gloomy.li: We'll cut it all and still be cold.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: foraging days
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Six days of taking in what the land grows by itself: each morning up to twelve wild plants ripe for picking within reach of the colony (berries, wild healroot, agave, mushrooms) are marked for the growers' harvest. A tribe's berry days, a village's gleaning of the hedges, an industrial or spacer colony's survey of the land's harvest: the baskets come in the same. Growers spend their mornings in the brush rather than the fields. Those with a love of plants and ascetics like it; undergrounders mind it.

effects.li: Each morning for six days, up to twelve wild plants ripe for picking within reach of the colony are marked for the growers' harvest, the nearest first (never a drug).
The growers spend their mornings picking them rather than in the fields.
Those with a love of plants and ascetics like it; undergrounders and the very industrious mind it.

plain.li: The bushes along the stream are heavy with berries and nobody's picking them.
[lowtech] My grandmother knew every bush within a day's walk, and so should we.
[!lowtech] Free food growing a short walk from the gate, and we buy ours from traders.

warm.li: A basket of berries every morning would make the whole colony smile.

cold.li: It's food that costs nothing but a walk.

plain.li: Picking berries when the field needs weeding.

gloomy.li: Half of it will be eaten by the birds before we get there.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: saving the power
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Five nights of saving the power: every lamp of the colony's is switched off at eleven at night and on again at five in the morning, except where a patient lies abed. The batteries carry the night with what the lamps would have burned. Anyone up in the night does it in the dark. Only for a colony on the grid; a tribe or a village banks its fires instead. Those who like the dark welcome it; night owls hate it, and the nervous mind it.

effects.li: Every lamp of the colony's is switched off from eleven at night to five in the morning (never one in a room with a patient abed), and on again as it was.
The batteries keep the power the lamps would have burned.
Those who like the dark, ascetics and undergrounders welcome it; night owls hate it, and the nervous mind it.

plain.li: The batteries are flat by dawn, and the lamps burn all night in empty rooms.
[industrial] Lights out at eleven, the way it was in the mill towns.
[spacer] Dim the habitat at night and the cells will last.

blunt.li: Nobody needs a lamp to sleep.

cold.li: Every lamp lit at three in the morning is power we'll want at noon.

plain.li: I do my best work at night, and now I'll do it in the dark.

gloomy.li: Something will come at the walls the one night it's dark.

cheerful.li: Fine, but I'm keeping a candle under my bed.

ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.label: every faith its evening
ColonyCouncil.DecreeDef.description: Ten days of the council treating every ideoligion in the colony alike: declared, the largest ideoligion that isn't the colony's own holds an evening of faith, and each morning those of other ideoligions trust the council a little more (the more open-minded the more) while the devout of the colony's own trust it a little less. It can't be declared while one ideoligion is named for the colony, nor that one while this holds. Only with Ideology and more than one ideoligion at home. Those of other ideoligions love it; the devout of the colony's own mind it.

effects.li: Declared, the largest ideoligion at home that isn't the colony's own holds an evening of faith, when one can be held.
Each morning those of other ideoligions trust the council a little more, the open-minded most; the devout of the colony's own ideoligion trust it a little less.
Those of other ideoligions love it and the kind like it; the devout of the colony's own mind it. Never together with one ideoligion for the colony.

plain.li: Half of us pray to something else, and the council should say that's welcome here.
[newcomer] The new ones don't share our ideoligion, and they should know they don't have to.

warm.li: Let every ideoligion here have its evening, and let's all be the better for it.

cold.li: People who feel welcome don't make trouble.

plain.li: The colony has an ideoligion, and the council should stand by it.

gloomy.li: Every faith its evening, and soon nobody keeps any of them.
